title: Open product decisions
objective: Resolve the product questions that gate later roadmap phases, recording each answer in docs/decisions.md and the affected specification.
context_summary: Accepted decisions live in docs/decisions.md. These tasks are the open questions: storage/backup workflow, RAW recording-mode and quality priorities, the first external module use case, accepted performance workloads and budgets, the Presence, colour mixer and vignette defaults, and interactive-preview quality levels beyond the authorized baseline.

tasks.description: Prioritize RAW work and define camera-specific quality expectations.
extra_context: RAW editing is implemented for the Nikon Z6, the Fujifilm X100VI and the supplied DJI Air 2S DNG, with neutral development as the initial direction; camera-look or Adobe matching is not selected (docs/decisions.md, Product and platform). Whether RAW precedes the tonal suite is settled by delivery, and the owner's private RAW manifest already feeds `raw-corpus`, `verify --manifest` and the `raw-editor` scenario.

Still open: which recording modes, firmware and controlled quality scenes to prioritise, how much camera JPEG or film-simulation matching matters beyond neutral, and whether lens correction, denoise or sharpening are essential (docs/decisions.md, Open product questions; docs/design/initial-raw.md, Remaining qualification and decisions). Bayer highlight latitude and the RAW memory budget have their own tasks in this plan.
The owner accepted this narrowing on 2026-09-28 (docs/decisions.md, "Plan refresh").

acceptance_criteria: Select one concrete extension the owner/community would use: preset, workflow automation, custom panel, decoder or processing tool.
Define its inputs/outputs, necessary permissions and customization/reset behavior.
Choose the smallest host boundary that supports the use case and defer a marketplace/general plugin runtime until justified.

Choose useful independent optional boundaries without assuming one binary per tool/camera; distinguish hidden panels, enabled features and loaded resources.

Define success as loading a separately authored module without host source changes and exposing its actions through the common APIs; an external client alone is insufficient.

tasks.description: Prioritize performance workloads and settle user-visible responsiveness goals.
extra_context: Record workload priorities and measured native M4 conditions; proposed performance budgets require evidence and owner acceptance.
Speed and lazy subsection editing within a full catalog are owner priorities. Avoid assuming binary splitting saves memory or latency.

Already accepted, and not reopened here: the slider-to-presented-frame target of 16 ms p95 with 32 ms acceptable (docs/decisions.md, Basic adjustments and histogram), shared working-memory budgets as targets that pace work rather than limits (Rendering memory), and the owner's 150 ms bound for the hold-`\` compare that chose the second RAW development (Post-consolidation review). The RAW process memory budget has its own task in this plan.

tasks.description: Refine the recorded defaults of the Presence, colour mixer and vignette proposals after reviewing the delivered work.
extra_context: The design records a default for every proposal so the plan can run without further input: Presence as the section name for Texture, Clarity and Dehaze; colour before spatial before geometry before finish with the mixer after Basic; three property groups for the mixer; one luminance-neutral vignette style; the spatial operation reading the quantized frame on the JPEG path; full-resolution drafts for spatial sliders with misses reported; the declared point-sample cost through a spatial layer.

Implementation was authorized on 2026-09-22 on the recorded defaults. A proposal is not a decision until the owner records it; until then the delivered behaviour follows the default and the design keeps calling it a proposal.

tasks.description: Choose measured quality levels and approximation-error limits for interactive viewport previews beyond the authorized baseline.
extra_context: Temporary softness at 100% during motion, full detail restored on pause/release, an updating full-image histogram, and the documented viewport-bounded clipping behavior are accepted and must not be reopened.

The documented implementation baseline uses a viewport window on a half-scale proxy while moving, then exact visible-region refinement and whole-frame exact analysis under the shared quiet policy. Further quality levels, GPU preview arithmetic and numerical error limits need representative measurements before acceptance; the sampled global guide is rejected due to severe periodic aliasing and no approximate-global mode ships.
Exact settled pixels, full-image reports and export retain their current contracts; product research does not imply an implementation latency result.
